rows.description: My parent shouts about my failure and I go quiet. I feel small. I can wait until things cool, then say I want to improve and ask for help with a plan.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, mockery, shame

rows.description: My teacher stays back to explain what I got wrong. I feel cared for. Accepting help is not weakness, and it shows that someone believes I can improve.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, mockery, shame

rows.description: A classmate laughs at my marks. It hurts, but I know one score does not define me. I can answer calmly or walk away, and remember that he too has weak spots.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, shame
related mind states: amusement, calm, hurt

rows.description: My friend says he also struggled and offers to study together. I feel less alone. Shared effort turns a failure into a team problem with a solution.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, mockery, shame

rows.description: After failing, I decide to practise the hard chapter every day. Growth starts when I look at mistakes without hating myself, and celebrate small improvements.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, mockery, shame

rows.description: I am scared of the dark and imagine things in the corner. Fear is real even if the danger is not. Talking about it and having a small light helps, and it fades with time.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: comfort, mockery

rows.description: My mother sits beside me after a nightmare and says I am safe. Her calm makes my heart slow down. I learn that fear shared becomes smaller.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, mockery
related mind states: fear, calm, trust

rows.description: A friend laughs that I am a scaredy-cat. It stings. Being afraid does not mean I am weak; I can say everyone is afraid of something, and choose friends who do not tease.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: comfort, fear

rows.description: I did something scary, like a swim or a stage show, and felt proud afterwards. Facing small fears builds trust in myself, and I do not need to prove bravery by risking safety.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: comfort, fear, mockery
related mind states: fear, pride, trust

rows.description: An older child threatens me and I am terrified. It is right to feel scared. I do not have to face it alone; telling a teacher or parent is smart, not shameful.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: comfort, fear, mockery
related mind states: fear, shame, shyness
